programme.desc: Tom Service introduces the classics of tomorrow in a special compilation performed at the classical music festival, with bold and brave compositions, illustrious orchestral pieces and more. Narrated by Gina McKee

programme.title: Tutankhamun: The Truth Uncovered
programme.desc: What killed Tutankhamun? Ever since the tomb of the boy king was discovered in 1922, he has become arguably the most famous pharaoh of all ancient Egypt. But his mysterious death at just 19 years of age has never been explained. Now, Dallas Campbell reveals new scientific research aimed at getting to the truth. A CT scan of the pharaoh's mummified body creates a full-size image of the real Tutankhamun, while DNA analysis uncovers a shocking secret about his family background - and the genetic trail leads to a revolutionary new theory about his sudden and unexpected death

programme.title: The Brits Who Designed the Modern World
programme.desc: Brenda Emmanus presents profiles of 10 celebrated British designers whose work has revolutionised the nation's homes, streets and culture since the Second World War. Among those whose careers are highlighted are road-sign designer Margaret Calvert, ZX Spectrum creator Rick Dickinson, Andrew Ritchie, who gave the world the Brompton Bike, and Kenneth Grange, who designed everything from British Rail's distinctive InterCity 125 to Kenwood food mixers. A panel of contributors including Will.i.am, Jeremy Paxman, Pete Waterman and Ade Adepitan explain how their lives have benefited from British designs

programme.title: The Murder Detective

Senior Investigating Officer Jason Murphy and his team begin the hunt for a masked gunman who seems to have disappeared without trace. With the murder weapon missing and not one of the 150 people on the street when Lyra was killed willing to come forward, detectives must painstakingly uncover the truth of what happened for themselves. Lyra's sister Nichola struggles with the devastating loss. As detectives uncover new evidence, the search for a single gunman grows into something much bigger, drawing Murphy towards investigating the leadership of the New IRA

programme.title: 24 Hours in A&E

programme.title: Love Cheats
programme.desc: The case of a man who told his girlfriend his life had been a series of tragedies, from his sister's death from cancer to losing his father to a hereditary heart condition that he in turn had developed. programme.title: The Murder Detective
programme.desc: Murphy and his team recover a gun that may be linked to Lyra McKee's murder. A DNA lead gives detectives their first direct route into the network surrounding the killing. Drawing on forensic evidence, intelligence, CCTV and mobile phone footage, detectives believe they can finally put a name to the masked figure at the centre of the case. Murphy launches a series of high-risk operations targeting those suspected of involvement. The stakes are immense. As the hunt enters a decisive new phase, Lyra's family's agonising wait for answers continues

programme.title: The Murder Detective
programme.desc: After years of investigation, arrests and painstaking evidence-gathering, lead detective Jason Murphy is ready to make his boldest move yet. Convinced that those responsible for Lyra's murder reach far beyond the gunman, Murphy targets the figures who he believes sit at the heart of the organisation behind the attack. With unprecedented access to never-before-seen tactical operations, cameras capture the high-stakes effort to turn years of intelligence and evidence into charges. Murphy's team execute a series of coordinated arrests but are faced with a wall of silence. The investigation gathers momentum with a gripping and emotional finale to an extraordinary seven-year investigation

programme.desc: The rugby player-turned-academic and mental health advocate sets out on an emotional quest to remember more than 1,300 people buried in unmarked graves in the grounds of the former St Loman's psychiatric hospital in his native Mullingar. He explores the burial practices of patients unclaimed after death and investigates how many more institutional graveyards there are like this around the country - and what can be done to respect and protect them

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Bob and Paul head off for a festive fishing trip to Norway, travelling to Vesteralen and the Lofoten Islands in the Arctic Circle and face a mighty maelstrom. The chain of islands is 1,000 miles north of Oslo and made up of majestic mountains, deep fjords and long, surf-swept beaches, and the pair are on a mission to find a variety of species including cod, halibut and pollock, and the ultimate prize, the hard-fighting coalfish. Along the way Bob surprises Paul with some unique accommodation in the most remote locations they have ever experienced, and the pair enjoy an array of culinary festive delights, including Christmas porridge and traditional Christmas cookies. programme.title: D-Day to Berlin
programme.desc: Sean Bean narrates the story of the behind-the-scenes battles between Dwight D Eisenhower and Field Marshal Montgomery toward the end of 1944. He describes how Anglo-American relations came under threat as the Allies fought in the conference chamber for the right to direct the final assault on Germany. Veterans from both sides describe the struggle to capture the bridge over the Rhine at Arnhem and the terrible winter conflicts during the Battle of the Bulge

programme.desc: Animals that live in Asia's deserts and dry grasslands, including the Gobi bear, one of the rarest animals on Earth who communicate by leaving their scent on ancient trees. programme.title: Asia
programme.desc: The series concludes with a look at the work of people striving to protect Asia's endangered wildlife, and what routes conservation could take in the future. In Japan, scientists take pregnant sharks, killed accidentally in fishing nets, and rescue their unborn young in an incubating system that simulates a womb. The programme also visits a village that used to be a hotbed of poaching and is now a centre for bird tourism

programme.title: Asia
programme.desc: David Attenborough narrates footage of the wildlife of Asia's forests. A Bengal tiger has her work cut out feeding three cubs, while greater one-horned rhinos battle it out in conflicts over territory. The rains of the monsoon prove an obstacle to a purple frog looking for a place to lay eggs, and a female orangutan in Borneo searches for a mate

programme.title: Asia
programme.desc: David Attenborough introduces footage of animals in Asia that live at extremely close quarters with people, from tigers making a home in town to elephants stopping traffic for food. A small park in central Bangkok supports 300 giant lizards, whilst a flying squirrel in Taipei has made a cosy home in a school. Proboscis monkeys are forced to venture uncomfortably closer to humans, and swifts in Jerusalem face tough competition for nest sites
